description: A granular tape recorder: audio is recorded onto a reel, the reel is cut into segments by markers, and grains are played back from the current segment under knob and CV control

params.text: Crossfades the output between the incoming audio fully left and reel playback fully right; while recording over existing audio in replace mode it also sets how much of the old recording is kept
Sets the length of the grain read from the current segment: the whole segment fully left, about 1ms fully right, on a fourth-power curve
Scales the voltage at the grain size CV input, -1 to +1, before it is added to the GRAIN knob
Sets playback speed and direction: stopped at centre, forward to twice speed fully right, backwards at about 4.5 times speed fully left, though the manual calls that end 26 semitones down
Scales the voltage at the speed CV input, -1 to +1, before it is added to the SPEED knob
Sets how much the grains overlap: gaps between them below 15%, one seamless grain to 35%, two voices to 50%, three with stereo panning to 70%, and four with random pitch above that
Offsets where in the current segment the grain is read from: the start of the segment fully left, as far in as the grain length allows fully right
Scales the voltage at the scan CV input, -1 to +1, before it is added to the SCAN knob
Steps through the markers on the reel and moves playback to the one chosen; its top value follows the number of markers and it reads out from 1
Pressing it starts recording the input onto the reel and pressing it again stops; with a cable in the clock input recording begins on the next clock edge instead of immediately
Pressing it drops a marker at the playback position, cutting another segment out of the reel
Pressing it moves playback to the next marker, wrapping round after the last one
Pressing it deletes every marker, sets the marker count back to four and returns SLCT to its first position
Pressing it spreads markers evenly across the reel, stepping through 4, 8 and 16 on successive presses
Sets what pressing REC does to audio already on the reel: replace wipes the reel and every marker first, overdub keeps them and adds the new audio from the playback position

inputs.text: The left audio input, recorded onto the reel and crossfaded to the output by MIX, with ±5V taken as full scale
The right audio input; with nothing patched here the left input feeds both channels
Shifts the MIX crossfade, 8V covering the whole of the knob's travel; the total of knob and voltage is held inside that travel
Shifts the grain length after scaling by its attenuverter, 8V covering the whole of the GRAIN knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the playback speed after scaling by its attenuverter, 4V covering the whole of the SPEED knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the grain overlap, 5V covering the whole of the DENS knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the scan offset after scaling by its attenuverter, 8V covering the whole of the SCAN knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the marker chosen by SLCT, 5V covering the whole run of markers; the total is held inside that run
A rising edge past 2.5V starts the next grain when DENS is below about half, or sets the grain length to the measured clock period above it
Playback runs while this is above 2.5V and stops at the end of the grain once it falls; with nothing patched it counts as held high
A rising edge past 2.5V starts recording, and the next one stops it
A rising edge past 2.5V drops a marker at the playback position
A rising edge past 2.5V moves playback to the next marker
A rising edge past 2.5V deletes every marker and returns SLCT to its first position
A rising edge past 2.5V spreads markers evenly across the reel, stepping through 4, 8 and 16 on successive edges

outputs.text: The left output: the incoming audio and the reel playback mixed by MIX at ±5V, or the expander's processed signal when one is fitted
The right output: the incoming audio and the reel playback mixed by MIX at ±5V, or the expander's processed signal when one is fitted
An envelope follower on the output, 0V in silence and rising to 8V at full level
A 10V pulse 1ms long at the end of every grain and every segment

notes: the reel is empty when the module is added, so nothing plays until you record onto it with REC or load a WAV file from the panel menu
the SPEED knob comes up at its centre, where playback is stopped, so a freshly added module is silent until it is moved off centre
clicking the waveform display drops a marker at that point, clicking an existing marker moves playback to it, and right-clicking a marker deletes it
a Tapestry Expander placed immediately to the right takes over the two audio outputs, feeding them through its bit crusher and filter
two buttons held together give extra actions: REC with NXT levels the incoming audio, and REC with MRK records into a new segment
NXT held with MRK deletes the current marker, and NXT held with REC deletes the audio of the current segment
holding NXT with MRK for 3 seconds deletes every marker, and holding NXT with REC for 3 seconds erases the whole reel
menu: Load Reel... — opens a file dialog and reads a WAV file onto the reel
Save Reel... — writes the reel out as a WAV file
Clear Reel — erases the recorded audio
Splice Count: 4 (click to cycle) — spreads that many markers evenly across the reel and steps the count on through 4, 8 and 16
Waveform Color: Red, Amber, Green, Baby Blue, Peach, Pink, White — sets the colour the recorded waveform is drawn in
